lesson.title: Arabic Heritage & Cultural Turns
lesson.subtitle: ojalá ('inshallah'), hasta ('hatta'), azul ('lazaward'), and la sobremesa

hook.title: Eight Centuries of Shared History in Your Mouth
hook.content: Between 711 and 1492, Arabic and Romance lived side by side on the Iberian Peninsula. Whenever you say **ojalá** ('hopefully / God willing'), **azul** ('blue'), **el limón** ('the lemon'), **el azúcar** ('sugar'), **la almohada** ('the pillow'), or **hasta** ('until', as in ¡Hasta mañana! / ¡Hasta luego!), you are speaking the living heritage of Al-Andalus!

pattern.title: La Sobremesa: The Untranslatable Art of Staying at the Table
pattern.content: And look at the Spanish compound **la sobremesa** (sobre 'over/after' + mesa 'table'): the cherished time spent lingering at the table talking with friends and family after the meal and coffee are finished!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: hopefully / God willing (Arabic law šá lláh)

exercises.target_answer: ojalá, azul, el limón, hasta mañana, la mesa
exercises.meaning: hopefully / God willing (Arabic law šá lláh), blue (Arabic lāzaward), lemon (Arabic līmūn + -ón), until tomorrow (Arabic ḥattā → hasta), the table (root of la sobremesa)
exercises.explanation: Arabic contributed roughly 4,000 words and expressions to Spanish.

exercises.prompt: Which everyday Spanish preposition meaning 'until' (as in '¡___ mañana!' and '¡___ la vista!') came from Arabic 'ḥattā'?
exercises.explanation: Arabic ḥattā became Old Spanish fasta and modern Spanish hasta (with silent h-)!

exercises.idea: say: 'Hopefully you have time to speak with my friend'
cues: time to (in order to) speak → tiempo para hablar
with my friend → con mi amigo
idea_parts: Hopefully you have time → Ojalá tengas tiempo
to speak with my friend → para hablar con mi amigo
exercises.target_answer: Ojalá tengas tiempo para hablar con mi amigo
exercises.meaning: I hope you have time to speak with my friend
exercises.explanation: ¡Ojalá tengas tiempo para hablar con mi amigo!

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: Agua con limón en la mesa azul
exercises.target_answer: Agua con limón en la mesa azul
exercises.meaning: Water with lemon on the blue table
cues: Water with lemon: Agua con limón
on the table: en la mesa
exercises.explanation: Agua con limón en la mesa azul — Latin and Arabic roots side by side!

summary.outcome: Recognize Arabic-heritage vocabulary (ojalá, azul, limón, hasta) and use it in full sentences.

use_example.german: ¡Adiós, hasta mañana — ojalá tengas un buen día!
use_example.english: Goodbye, until tomorrow — I hope you have a great day!

summary.takeaway: Spanish is a tapestry of Latin structure and rich historical layers including Arabic and Greek.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([30] Capstone: El Puente Reading): bring all 30 topics together in a connected Madrid narrative!

ojalá.english_meaning: hopefully, I hope that, if only (always triggers subjunctive!)
ojalá.context_translation: I hope you have a great day!
ojalá.etymology_derivation: Direct Arabic inheritance in Spanish; always triggers the subjunctive mood (tengas, venga, sea)!

azul.etymology_derivation: Hispano-Arabic lāzaward ('lapis lazuli') → azul. English azure is the exact same word.

limón.etymology_derivation: In Spanish, la lima is the smaller green lime, and el limón (-ón augmentative) is the larger yellow lemon!

café.etymology_derivation: Turkish kahve → Italian caffè → Spanish café. An international word shared across Europe.

mesa.context_translation: I want to reserve a table.
mesa.etymology_derivation: Latin mēnsa ('table') gave Spanish la mesa — which English borrowed in the American Southwest for a flat-topped 'table' mountain!

tener.etymology_derivation: Latin tenēre ('to hold'). While other tongues used 'have' (like French avoir), Spanish promoted 'hold' (tener) to main possession.

tengo.etymology_derivation: Latin teneō developed an epenthetic velar g: tengo.

hablar.english_meaning: to speak, to talk (hablo: I speak)
hablar.etymology_derivation: Latin fabulārī (to converse, tell stories — English fable and fabulous) shifted initial f- to silent h-: hablar!

mañana.context_translation: Tomorrow I am going to work.
mañana.etymology_derivation: As an adverb (mañana) it means 'tomorrow'; as a feminine noun (la mañana) it means 'the morning' (mañana por la mañana = 'tomorrow morning')!
